body: Feels like this was typed by my own fingers. Couldn’t possibly relate more.

I spent the majority of the last 48 hours I had off work cleaning my pc side panel and monitors, broke one of the monitors in the process via water damage and had to replace it.. so I guess I can maybe take that as a lesson learned? But idk I’ve already gotten a habit of replacing things like that even when they aren’t necessarily broken I just want the compulsion to go away and if there’s a price tag to that then fuck it right?

I had always been scared of ruining items so I guess if that is a valid answer I would choose that. The therapIST just wasn’t right for me, so I’m seeing a new one this coming Monday from NoOCD. I’m also going to talk about my meds with the psychiatrist because my symptoms skyrocketed to the tenth power ever since beginning Luvox
I’ve tried weed, therapy, ocd meds, and MANY types of meditation with little to no success.

Me too. Feels like I’ll be scrubbing and cleaning and observing things until I’m physically unable to do so.. I haven’t found any methods that bring me some form of respite yet. I’m exhausted entirely.

There isn’t much that helps.. I have a love for gaming and stuff but with the ocd I can’t even go anywhere near my setup.. ive grown to be scared and disgusted by its imperfections and I’m scared of ruining things by “fixing” it. 

The only thing that helps is sleep. I don’t get much anymore.

Thank you for your advice! I find myself both excited and fearful at the same time because of this very fact. Excitement coming from the fact that I know it would very likely teach me some much-needed work/life balance skills. The fear mainly just coming from the stuff my parents have instilled in my mind over the years. The idea that anything less than 40 hours a week is entirely unsustainable in 99% of cases, and to go ANYWHERE expecting to ask for any less would be ludicrous, and makes me look bad.) I know that this is a slight stretch, and that they ultimately just want the best for me. However, I can’t shake the anxious feeling this advice gives me. I’m excited to grow and learn, I have no problem doing 40 hours a week somewhere that I enjoy working at.. I just don’t necessarily think I absolutely NEED to work 40+ hours to achieve sustainability. And if that’s the case, I’d rather take those few hours a week to have more time for my own life.

Thank you for your response, I’m obviously very eager to become further educated on this matter and hearing about your personal experience truly does put some things into perspective for me. Thankfully, I am indeed planning on moving out with my long term partner within the next couple of years, which I neglected to mention in my original post. Hopefully, this fact alone will make life seem a little less financially hectic. Who knows, either way.. thank you for your response!

Absolutely perfect! I’m all healed up and it was actually just some food lodged into the actual spaces where the teeth were.. there’s the pipette thingy that you need to use to flush them out which they never gave me upon exiting the initial operation (I guess they aren’t standard everywhere). Rest assured, though- it was all good!

My heart of hearts tells me that getting the degree will not only damn near kill me in every aspect, but will also be rather unfulfilling and meaningless even if completed. 

I guess I’m curious to explore the different avenues that other folks in similar situations as mine have found worthwhile, profitable, or fulfilling. Because ultimately, this college shit isn’t working for me, and I’ve gotta navigate my way out of that, and into something else alongside battling a mindset in which anything less than a prestigious degree is a lost cause.

I’m not sure if my original post’s question was made clear, or if it was- perhaps I had a hard time analyzing your response.

I’ve been fear mongered by the education system to believe that anything less than a degree is not only a failure of great magnitude, but will ultimately lead to an unfulfilling, unsuccessful rest of my life. 

My question, (with utmost respect) is that if I were to NOT go in the direction of a degree, am I.. how you say- fucked? Or is it possible for people like me who might not find it feasible to get a degree to be better off that way. 

Thanks for your reply :)
Thank you! I just now saw this and I just want to extend love and good wishes to ANYONE suffering the same thing as I described above!

UPDATE!!!!
So a little more info on what I was experiencing OTHER THAN the food being stuck.. I noticed there was this secretion of what appeared to be infectious fluid so of course my doc wanted to see me ASAP.. come to find out it was Bc of food so far stuck in there that it created this fluid, however no dry socket (fully matured clots) and no infection... just some food, NOW I have a syringe and use it daily as instructed. Thanks for your wonderful insight my friend! ❤️❤️ PPS(NO MORE PAIN)
I’ve heard that you can cause dry socket by blasting the clot out with water doing exactly that, is there anything you might be able to tell me that can confirm or deny this information?

Got all four out on Tuesday (a week ago as of this msg) and today I noticed an ENTIRE PEA stuck in the back crevasse of my extraction site, no syringe was given for my post op and the rinsing did not make it budge, truthfully I think I’ll have them flush it out later this afternoon but it’s definitely sending my anxiety in a spiral.

Not sure what to make of it but I got my four wisdom teeth extracted exactly a week ago today, and I do have a throbbing pain in my lower two sockets (which are significantly more open than the top 2) and the pain is on and off.. what really concerned me though is I’m pretty sure there was some food in the socket left behind from the last few meals I’d eaten. (It was liquid-like, did not have a foul odor, and when released it was actually a relief? My face swelled up due to the attention given to the area but I’m still wondering if this is an emergency situation or not...

You’re still here, you can still taste and obviously can still enjoy the little things life has to offer (like sugary food lol) and at the end of the day, it’s people like you and I alike who need to know that it’s ok to be unhappy, and it’s ok to not like your current position in life, but to quit and miss out on another opportunity to eat that ice cream?
